questions.q: Who was one of the gatekeepers descended from Korah?
questions.a: Meshelemiah, the son of Kore, was one of the gatekeepers descended from Korah.

questions.q: How many sons did Meshelemiah have?
questions.a: Meshelemiah had seven sons.

questions.q: How many sons did Obed Edom have?
questions.a: Obed Edom had eight sons, because God blessed him.

questions.q: What did Shemaiah’s sons become in their father’s house?
questions.a: They became leaders because they were capable men.

questions.q: How many capable sons and brothers were there from the family of Obed Edom?
questions.a: There were 62 capable, strong men, able to serve at the temple.

questions.q: How many capable sons and brothers did Meshelemiah have?
questions.a: Meshelemiah had 18 capable sons and brothers.

questions.q: How many capable sons and brothers came from the family of Hosah, a descendant of Merari?
questions.a: Altogether, there were 13 sons and relatives from the family of Hosah.

questions.q: Where were these divisions of Levites responsible to serve?
questions.a: They were responsible to serve in Yahweh’s house guarding the gates and storehouses.

questions.q: How did the Israelite leaders decide which family group would guard each gate?
questions.a: They cast lots to decide which family group would guard each gate.

questions.q: Which gates did the lots assign to Shelemiah and his son Zechariah?
questions.a: The lot assigned Shelemiah to guard the east gate and Zechariah to guard the north gate.

questions.q: What was assigned to Obed Edom’s sons in addition to the south gate?
questions.a: His sons were assigned the storehouses.

questions.q: Which gate were Shuppim and Hosah assigned to guard?
questions.a: They were assigned to guard the west gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the road leading up to the temple.

questions.q: How many Levites guarded the east, north, and south gates each day?
questions.a: Six Levites guarded the east gate, four guarded the north and four the south gates each day.

questions.q: How many Levites guarded the west side?
questions.a: Four Levites guarded the road on the west side and two guarded the courtyard.

questions.q: Which family groups made up the divisions of the gatekeepers?
questions.a: The divisions of the gatekeepers were made up of the descendants of Korah and the descendants of Merari.

questions.q: What was Ahijah in charge of in the house of God?
questions.a: He was in charge of the treasures of God’s house and of the treasures of the dedicated things.

questions.q: Who was one of the leaders among Ladan’s descendants?
questions.a: Jehieli was one of the leaders among Ladan’s descendants.

questions.q: Who was in charge of the treasuries of the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: Zetham and his brother Joel, the sons of Jehieli, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: Who was appointed as leader over the treasuries?
questions.a: Shebuel, a descendant of Moses through Gershom, was appointed as leader over the treasuries.

questions.q: Who was Shelomoth descended from?
questions.a: Shelomoth was descended from Eliezer, Moses’ other son, through Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, and Zichri.

questions.q: What were Shelomoth and his brothers in charge of?
questions.a: They were in charge of all the treasuries of the holy things that King David and the army commanders had dedicated.

questions.q: For what purpose was some of the plunder won in battles dedicated by David and the commanders?
questions.a: They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to help maintain Yahweh’s house.

questions.q: Whose dedicated items were under the care of Shelomoth and his brothers?
questions.a: The items dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul, Abner, and Joab were under the care of Shelomoth and his brothers.

questions.q: What were Chenaniah and his sons in charge of as officials and judges?
questions.a: They were in charge of the civil affairs of Israel as officials and judges.

questions.q: What did Hashabiah and his 1,700 relatives oversee?
questions.a: They oversaw the Israelites west of the Jordan River, doing the work of Yahweh and serving the king.

questions.q: When were capable warriors found among Hebron’s descendants in Jazer of Gilead?
questions.a: They were found in the fortieth year of David’s reign.

questions.q: Which tribes did King David appoint Jerijah’s 2,700 relatives to oversee?
questions.a: King David appointed them over the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of the tribe of Manasseh.

commentary.text: —The porters and treasurers of the temple, had occasion for strength and valour to oppose those who wrongly attempted to enter the sanctuary, and to guard the sacred treasures. Much was expended daily upon the altar; flour, wine, oil, salt, fuel, beside the lamps; quantities of these were kept beforehand, besides the sacred vestments and utensils. These were the treasures of the house of God. These treasures typified the plenty there is in our heavenly Father's house, enough and to spare. From those sacred treasuries, the unsearchable riches of Christ, all our wants are supplied; and receiving from his fulness, we must give him the glory, and endeavour to dispose of our abilities and substance according to his will. We have an account of those employed as officers and judges. The magistracy is an ordinance of God for the good of the church, as truly as the ministry, and must not be neglected. None of the Levites who were employed in the service of the sanctuary, none of the singers or porters, were concerned in this outward business; one duty was enough to engage the whole man. Wisdom, courage, strength of faith, holy affections, and constancy of mind in doing our duty, are requisite or useful for every station.
